Note (1): The lines of Sugar (1969, J. Res. Natl. Bur. Stand. 73A, 333;
    DOI:10.6028/jres.073A.029) above 47540 cm-1 and of Sugar (1974, J. Res.
    Natl. Bur. Stand. 78A, 555; DOI:10.6028/jres.078A.036) below 47441 cm-1; the
    two lists do not overlap. Every line Sugar printed is given once, including
    the lines of intensity 0 (the hyperfine components he listed in 1974), which
    are given without classification. A line with several classifications has
    one row for each; its observed quantities are repeated on each row. Rows are
    in order of increasing wavelength.
Note (2): Computed from wn_obs: in standard air below 50000 cm-1, with the
    dispersion formula of Peck and Reeder (1972, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 62, 958;
    DOI:10.1364/JOSA.62.000958), in vacuum above.
Note (3): As estimated in this work (Supplementary Information). For the lines
    of intensity 0, Sugar's nominal uncertainty for 1974 (0.003 Angstrom, 0.007
    Angstrom for lines with a character).
Note (4): Where Sugar's uncertainty is increased individually: his value and the
    increased one, in Angstrom, e.g., 0.003->0.013.
Note (5): Sugar's wavenumber in vacuum, as adopted in this work (see the E
    notes).
Note (6): Sugar's intensity as interpreted in this work (see the E notes).
Note (7): Sugar's line character as he gave it; an asterisk is appended to the
    character of a line with more than one classification in this work.
Note (8): Sugar's intensity converted to a linear scale and corrected for the
    spectral response (Supplementary Information); blank for the lines of
    intensity 0.
Note (9): Level identifiers of Supplementary Data 2. Original classifications
    are those of Sugar (1969, 1974) or Wyart, with the corrections given in the
    E notes; those of this work are the accepted ones.
Note (10): Calculated intensity on the scale of I_cor, from the gA of DREAM
    (Supplementary Information).
Note (11): With the Ritz wavenumber from the energies E_W99 of Supplementary
    Data 2, in the same medium as wl_obs.
Note (12): From the uncertainty of gA given by DREAM: ln(1 + u(gA)/gA).
Note (13): Blank where DREAM gives no value.
Note (14): The fraction of the observed intensity attributed to this transition:
    its share of the calculated intensities of the line's classifications in
    this work (1/n where an intensity is missing). It weights the line in the
    level optimization.
Note (15): From the energies E_opt of Supplementary Data 2, optimized with LOPT;
    in the same medium as wl_obs.
Note (16): Codes as follows (several are separated by commas):
      N  = new classification (not among the original ones of the line);
      R  = original classification revised: not accepted in this work,
           where the line has another classification;
      D  = original classification discarded: the line has none in this
           work;
      Q  = involves a level marked questionable in Supplementary Data 2;
      En = correction of Sugar's data or other remark, as follows:
      E1 = Sugar's wavenumber 97867.0 is corrected to 97870.0, which agrees with
           his wavelength.
      E2 = Sugar's wavenumbers of 96608.00, 95652.88 and 91974.99 disagreed with
           his wavelengths (by about 0.9, 1.8 and 0.9 cm-1) and are corrected to
           agree with them.
      E3 = The original classifications involving the level 059003.000098 are
           Wyart's (Wyart, Blaise and Camus 1974, Phys. Scr. 9, 325;
           DOI:10.1088/0031-8949/9/6/004).
      E4 = Sugar's wavenumber 92856.0 is corrected to 92859.0, which agrees with
           his wavelength.
      E5 = Sugar's wavenumber 84612.0 is corrected to 84613.0, which agrees with
           his wavelength.
      E6 = Sugar's classifications involving the level 88220.2 o 9/2 of NIST ASD
           are omitted: Wyart rejected that level and replaced it by 88210.1
           (059003.000304). Lines and their lower levels: 48349.80 (39870.17),
           53195.88 (35024.49), 56965.61 (31254.71), 65692.62 (22527.70; Sugar's
           second classification of this line), 66685.08 (21535.17), 66925.44
           (21294.89), 72084.12 (16135.97).
      E7 = Sugar's classifications involving the level 46673.78 e 7/2 of NIST
           ASD are omitted: Wyart rejected that level and replaced it by
           46783.64 (059003.000184). Lines and their other levels: 19694.12
           (26979.66 o 9/2), 66485.57 (113158.8 o 9/2), 68747.32 (115420.8 o
           7/2).
      E8 = Sugar's J = 5/2 of the upper level 69138.28 is corrected to 9/2.
      E9 = Sugar's J = 7/2 of the lower level 15045.8 is corrected to 5/2.
      E10 = Sugar's wavenumber 53163.5 is corrected to 53165.5, which agrees
            with his wavelength.
      E11 = Sugar listed this line twice; it is given once.
      E12 = Sugar's classification 24309.20 e - 68331.73 o 7/2 is forbidden (J =
            3/2 for the lower level); replaced by 24470.90-68492.43
            (059003.000105-059003.000245).
      E13 = Sugar printed the classification 36670.57-79136.23 on 42462.15; it
            fits 42465.58, where it is given.
      E14 = Sugar printed the classification 30994.55-67870.76 on 36875.76; it
            fits 36875.87, where it is given.
      E15 = Sugar printed intensity 5, character c and the classification of
            33540.70; taken as an intensity-0 line, the repeated classification
            omitted.
      E16 = Sugar gives intensity 0 (an hfs component) with the classification
            35291.00-68238.12; intensity 10 and character bl are assigned to
            keep his classification in this work.
      E17 = Sugar's classification, a repetition of that of 32530.39
            (35801.12-68331.73), is replaced by 27604.26-60166.20
            (059003.000123-059003.000196).
      E18 = Sugar's wavenumber 32382.56 is replaced by 32382.67, recomputed from
            his wavelength 3087.175; it is much closer to his Ritz wavenumber.
      E19 = Sugar printed the classification 35384.17-66943.04 on 31604.54
            (intensity 4, character c), 45.7 cm-1 from its Ritz wavenumber; it
            is given on 31558.08, and 31604.54 is taken as intensity 0 without
            character.
      E20 = Sugar gives intensity 0 (an hfs component) with the classification
            37919.58-68544.19; intensity 2 and character bl are assigned to keep
            his classification in this work.
      E21 = Sugar printed the classification 18693.65-34198.61
            (059003.000065-059003.000143) on 15505.05; it fits 15504.95, where
            it is given.
      E22 = Sugar printed the classification 18693.65-32288.92
            (059003.000065-059003.000138) on 13595.34; it fits 13595.21, where
            it is given.
      E23 = Sugar's classification 41023 e 7/2 - 54184 o 5/2 (his level values)
            is omitted: the upper level is neither in NIST ASD nor in W99.
      E24 = Sugar printed 11477.67 with intensity 20 and with the classification
            of 11477.77 (9370.66-20848.39); its intensity is set to 0 and the
            repeated classification omitted; 11477.77, printed without a
            character, is given the character *r.
Note (17): Codes as follows (paper 2: A. Kramida, to be published):
      A2 = a line Sugar printed that is missing from this list as a line;
           added in paper 2;
      R2 = revised in paper 2: Sugar's intensity, character or
           classification;
      L2 = Sugar's printed hfs component made a line in paper 2;
      M2 = merged with another line in paper 2;
      C2 = identified as an hfs companion in paper 2.
